canonical_data: routing records, task trajectories and learned patterns with embeddings in a local SQLite database, plus a generated .claude folder of settings, agent definitions and commands in the project
current_repo_note: The repository root has no licence file although the readme links to one; the MIT grant is recorded in the root and package manifests, and several nested packages and example folders carry their own MIT texts under other copyright names.
strengths: Routing, edit and command outcomes are written to a local SQLite store of trajectories, patterns and routings that later hook calls read back to suggest an agent, which is state a prompt kit does not keep

One command writes a Claude Code settings file with pre-edit, post-edit and pre-command hooks plus agent definitions and slash commands, and the same functions are exposed as MCP tools and a TypeScript API
Background workers are dispatched from keywords in prompts and deposit findings into memory, under a resource governor
weaknesses: The repository root has no licence file although the readme says to see one; the MIT grant rests on package manifests and nested per-package texts under different copyright names
The pre-command risk hook computes blocked and approved flags but the command always exits zero, so it advises rather than denies

The orchestration runtime keeps run status in memory and delegates to an external command, while the readme's headline figures for speed-ups, quality gains and agent counts are the author's own and were not reproduced
The repository mixes a v2 package with an older root manifest, committed tarballs and database files, and a submodule pointer, which makes the shipped surface hard to delimit
why_it_matters: A widely starred attempt to turn Claude Code into a self-routing multi-agent setup through hooks and a learning store, useful as a case study in how much of such a stack is state and how much is claim.
